question: Which top-level packaging containers, meaning those not contained within any other packaging, have any item for which the total quantity accumulated across all nested levels in the hierarchy exceeds 500, and what are the names of both these containers and the corresponding items?
sql:
-- The results look correct. Let me verify the calculations one more time:
-- 
-- Pallet of L (531):
--   531 -> 521 (Box Large) qty=12, 521 -> 502 (Bottle 500cl) qty=72
--   Total: 12 * 72 = 864 ✓ (> 500)
--
-- Pallet of M (532):
--   532 -> 522 (Box Medium) qty=20, 522 -> 501 (Bottle 330cl) qty=36
--   Total: 20 * 36 = 720 ✓ (> 500)
--
-- Pallet Mix MS (533):
--   533 -> 522 (Box Medium) qty=10, 522 -> 501 (Bottle 330cl) qty=36 → 10*36 = 360 (< 500, excluded)
--   533 -> 523 (Box Small) qty=20, 523 -> 502 (Bottle 500cl) qty=30 → 20*30 = 600 ✓ (> 500)
--
-- Pallet Mix SG (534):
--   534 -> 523 (Box Small) qty=20, 523 -> 502 (Bottle 500cl) qty=30 → 20*30 = 600
--   534 -> 524 (Gift Box) qty=16, 524 -> 511 (Gift Carton) qty=8, 511 -> 501 (Bottle 330cl) qty=3 → 16*8*3 = 384 (< 500)
--   534 -> 524 (Gift Box) qty=16, 524 -> 511 (Gift Carton) qty=8, 511 -> 502 (Bottle 500cl) qty=2 → 16*8*2 = 256
--   Total for 502: 600 + 256 = 856 ✓ (> 500)
--   Total for 501: 384 (< 500, excluded)
--
-- All calculations check out. The answer is correct.

-- But wait - the question says "total quantity accumulated across all nested levels" - 
-- should I also consider intermediate packaging levels as "items"? 
-- The question says "items" and the leaf items are bottles. Let me re-read:
-- "Which top-level packaging containers... have any item for which the total quantity accumulated across all nested levels in the hierarchy exceeds 500"
-- 
-- "Items" here likely refers to the leaf-level packaging items (bottles), since those are the actual products/items being packaged.
-- The current answer filters to leaf items only, which seems correct.
-- 
-- Let me submit this result.
SELECT 
    h.top_name as container_name,
    p.name as item_name,
    SUM(h.level_qty) as total_qty
FROM (
    WITH RECURSIVE hierarchy AS (
        SELECT 
            p.id as top_id,
            p.name as top_name,
            pr.contains_id,
            pr.qty as level_qty,
            1 as depth
        FROM packaging p
        JOIN packaging_relations pr ON pr.packaging_id = p.id
        WHERE p.id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT contains_id FROM packaging_relations)
        
        UNION ALL
        
        SELECT 
            h.top_id,
            h.top_name,
            pr.contains_id,
            h.level_qty * pr.qty as level_qty,
            h.depth + 1
        FROM hierarchy h
        JOIN packaging_relations pr ON pr.packaging_id = h.contains_id
    )
    SELECT top_id, top_name, contains_id, level_qty FROM hierarchy
) h
JOIN packaging p ON p.id = h.contains_id
WHERE p.id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
GROUP BY h.top_id, h.top_name, h.contains_id, p.name
HAVING SUM(h.level_qty) > 500
ORDER BY h.top_name, p.name;

            1 as depth
        FROM packaging p
        JOIN packaging_relations pr ON pr.packaging_id = p.id
        WHERE p.id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT contains_id FROM packaging_relations)
        
        UNION ALL
        
        SELECT 
            h.top_id,
            h.top_name,
            pr.contains_id,
            h.level_qty * pr.qty as level_qty,
            h.depth + 1
        FROM hierarchy h
        JOIN packaging_relations pr ON pr.packaging_id = h.contains_id
    )
    SELECT top_id, top_name, contains_id, level_qty FROM hierarchy
) h
JOIN packaging p ON p.id = h.contains_id
WHERE p.id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT packaging_id FROM packaging_relations)
GROUP BY h.top_id, h.top_name, h.contains_id, p.name
HAVING SUM(h.level_qty) > 500
ORDER BY h.top_name, p.name;
